elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 13 retains automatic renewal ("This Agreement shall renew automatically thereafter for successive one year periods") and the redline does not convert renewal to mutual written agreement, so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied; the reminder and CPI/3% cap elements are not, so this element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 13: renewal is "for successive one year periods" — a 12-month renewal term, unchanged by the redline.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 13 permits Client to deliver "written notice of intent not to renew no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year"; the inserted sentence restates the same 30-day window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No renewal reminder obligation appears anywhere in Section 13, Section 6 or the inserted sentence; the drafter concedes this in the rationale. To meet it, an operative TrueLink obligation to notify Client at least 60 days before each renewal date would be required.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence caps increases at "more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term" — a flat 5%, not the lesser of CPI and 3%.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13 requires notice of intent not to renew "no later than thirty (30) days prior to the end of said year" (30 ≤ 60); the inserted sentence repeats "Client's non-renewal notice window under this Section 13 is 30 days". The deterministic regex reporting "number not found" is a matcher artefact — the 30-day figure is present in substance in both the retained and inserted text.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative sentence: "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term." This closes the gap left by Section 6, whose freeze runs only "for a period of one year from the date of this Agreement".

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the retained Section 13 30-day non-renewal window already sits inside the 60-day ceiling, and the inserted flat 5% cap on renewal-term fee increases fills the pricing gap left by the one-year-only freeze in Section 6. The 'deviation' classification is correct because, absent the insertion, renewal pricing was uncapped and the fallback failed on a material term.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no TrueLink obligation to remind Client at least 60 days before renewal, and the cap is a flat 5% rather than the lesser of CPI and 3%. These are recorded as unpressed preferred sub-elements, not as separate defects.

Minimality fails on duplication. The 30-day non-renewal window is already an operative term of Section 13 and required no amendment; the clause "For clarity, Client's non-renewal notice window under this Section 13 is 30 days" restates an existing operative covenant that was already compliant. Repair: delete that leading clause and let the insertion read only "TrueLink's fees will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term."

Intent is preserved: the Section 6 first-year freeze and most-favoured-rate covenant, the Sections 2/3 early-termination provisos, the Section 12 termination cross-reference and the 30/60-day name-server and hosting-migration deadlines all survive intact, and confining the cap to "any renewal term" avoids any conflict with the first-year freeze. No undefined terms or dangling cross-references are created.

Optional tightening (not a defect at fallback): "will not increase by more than five percent (5%) in any renewal term" could be read cumulatively; "by more than five percent (5%) over the fees in effect during the immediately preceding term" would remove the ambiguity.
